id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

from.description: The starting position in the relation.

to.description: The ending position in the relation.

points.description: The points that are used to draw the line between the `from` and `to` assets.

facilities.description:
The facilities that are associated with this relation.
This is used to filter the relations based on the facilities.

If both {@link ReliabilityAsset} belongs to the same facility, then #facilities will contain a single element.
but if they belong to a different facility, then #facilities will contain both the facilities.

title:
Represents the relationship between a {@link ReliabilityAsset}s in a geographical map.
This is used to generate the map view of the asset under "Asset Map" page.

This relation is "valid" whenever it meets the following conditions:
- The `from` and `to` are different.
- The `from` and `to` are {@link ReliabilityAsset}s with [geographical locations](ReliabilityAsset#geoLocation) data.

Additionally this entity has a `points` field which is used to store the points that are used to draw the line
between the `from` and `to` assets, in case the relation is not a direct line.

For example, the following diagram shows a relations between 3 assets:
```
 Asset 0        @────@
  ▲   ▲         │    │
  │   │         │    │
  │   @─────────@    │
  │                  ▼
  │               Asset 2
  │
  │
  │
  ▼
Asset 1
```

In this case, `Asset 0 --> Asset 1` has no `points`(`@`) and is a direct line. While `Asset 0 --> Asset 2` has
4 `points`(`@`) and is not a direct line.

**NOTE**: All the connections in this graph are bidirectional, meaning that you can create a single relation
          between `Asset 0` and `Asset 1` and it will be used to represent the connection in both directions.
name: ReliabilityMapAssetRelation
